title: Open fibred subcategories inherit algebraicity and local finite presentation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal Y$ an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and $j:\mathcal U\to\mathcal Y$ a morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes. Suppose that for every scheme-valued object $T\to\mathcal Y$, the two-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal U$ is represented over $T$ by an open subscheme [def-sfb-open-moduli-substack]. Then $\mathcal U$ is an algebraic stack. If $\mathcal Y\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, so is $\mathcal U\to S$. Here locally of finite presentation means that a smooth surjective scheme atlas has locally finitely presented structural composite [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 05UN, lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic; stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 06Q7, lemma-open-immersion-locally-finite-presentation, and 06Q3, lemma-composition-finite-presentation.

proof.text: For every $T\to\mathcal Y$, the hypothesis supplies a scheme representing $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal U$, namely its specified open subscheme of $T$. The algebraic-stack definition makes $\mathcal Y$ an etale stack. Apply the scheme-representable fibred-category descent theorem with $\mathcal F=\mathcal U$, $\mathcal G=\mathcal Y$ and $q=j$. It follows that $\mathcal U$ is an etale stack; no stack assumption on $\mathcal U$ or surjectivity of $j$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic), stack assertion, specialized to scheme fibres and the etale convention

proof.text: The open-fibre hypothesis also makes $j$ fully faithful on each fibre. Fix $x,x'\in\mathcal U(T)$ and $\alpha:j(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}j(x')$. In $h_T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal U$, formed using $j(x):h_T\to\mathcal Y$, consider $(\mathrm{id}_T,x,1)$ and $(\mathrm{id}_T,x',\alpha)$. Under its representing equivalence they give sections of an open immersion $W\to T$. Monomorphy of that immersion says the sections are equal. In a discrete represented groupoid equal sections have exactly one arrow between them; full faithfulness of the representing equivalence therefore gives exactly one arrow between these two triples. The 2-fibre-product arrow equation says precisely that this arrow is $a:x\to x'$ with $j(a)=\alpha$. Thus every $\alpha$ lifts uniquely, naturally under restriction.

source.place: Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic); open-fibre specialization, using schemes.tex Tag 01L7 (lemma-immersions-monomorphisms)

proof.text: Check the diagonal of $\mathcal U$ on a scheme $T\to\mathcal U\times_S\mathcal U$, specified by $x,x'\in\mathcal U(T)$. Its 2-fibre is equivalent to the discrete functor $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal U}(x,x')$: over $V\to T$ the triple $(u,a:u\xrightarrow{\sim}x|_V,b:u\xrightarrow{\sim}x'|_V)$ maps to $ba^{-1}$, with inverse $\beta\mapsto(x|_V,1,\beta)$. The arrow $a$ identifies the other composite with the identity. By step 2, applying $j$ gives a restriction-compatible bijection with $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y}(jx,jx')$. The same explicit equivalence identifies this last functor with the scheme test of $\Delta_{\mathcal Y}$ at $(jx,jx')$, which is an algebraic space by algebraicity of $\mathcal Y$. This provides an algebraic-space representative for every scheme test of $\Delta_{\mathcal U}$.

source.place: Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), (1) iff (2), with the fibre equivalence written out

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:A\to\mathcal Y$. By hypothesis $A\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal U$ is equivalent over $A$ to an open subscheme $W\subseteq A$. The other projection $W\to\mathcal U$ is the 2-base change of $p$. The representable fibred-groupoid smooth calculus makes it representable by algebraic spaces, smooth and surjective. Together with steps 1 and 3 this is exactly an algebraic-stack structure on $\mathcal U$: etale descent, representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas.

source.place: Tag 05UM (lemma-representable-morphism-to-algebraic), atlas construction; Tags 0302 and 045C for arbitrary 2-base change

proof.text: The scheme inclusion $i:W\hookrightarrow A$ is locally of finite presentation directly from the definitions. At each $w\in W$, choose an affine open neighbourhood $V\subseteq A$ contained in the open image of $W$. The restriction $i^{-1}V\to V$ is an isomorphism by the definition of open immersion, so the corresponding ring map is an isomorphism. It is finitely presented as an algebra with zero generators and zero relations, after this identification. These affine neighbourhoods verify local finite presentation at every point; if $W$ is empty the condition is vacuous.

Now assume $\mathcal Y\to S$ is locally of finite presentation in the atlas sense stated in the item. Choose the atlas $A\to\mathcal Y$ in step 4 so that $A\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. Step 5 and composition of locally finitely presented scheme maps give that $W\to A\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. The atlas $W\to\mathcal U$ of step 4, with this structural composite, witnesses exactly the asserted local finite presentation of $\mathcal U\to S$.

source.place: Tag 01TR (lemma-composition-finite-presentation), applied to the pulled-back open atlas; stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 06Q2 and 06Q3

lean.statement: theorem openStackAlgebraicLfp {S : Scheme.{u}} (U : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)) (Y : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)) (j : BasedFunctor U Y) (hU : IsFibredInGroupoids U) (hY : IsAlgebraicModuliStack Y) (hOpen : ∀ (T : Over S) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) Y), ∃ (W : Over S) (i : W ⟶ T), IsOpenImmersion i.left ∧ ∃ e : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj W)) (moduliTwoFiberProduct t j), e.toFunctor.IsEquivalence ∧ Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (e.comp (moduliTwoFiberFst t j)) (discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map i)))) : IsAlgebraicModuliStack U ∧ ((∃ (A : Over S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj A)) Y), IsSmoothModuliAtlas Y A a ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation A.hom) → ∃ (W : Over S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj W)) U), IsSmoothModuliAtlas U W a ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation W.hom)
